title: Permutation sign as an ordered-pair product
statement: Let $n\geq0$ be an integer and let $\sigma$ be a permutation, that is, a bijection of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ with itself. Write $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\in\{1,-1\}\subset\mathbf Z$ for the permutation sign defined in [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], the group homomorphism taking every transposition to $-1$ (using indices starting at zero). Then $$\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\ \prod_{i<j<n}\begin{cases}1&\sigma(i)<\sigma(j),\\-1&\sigma(i)>\sigma(j).\end{cases}$$ The empty product is $1$, so this includes $n=0$ and $n=1$.
